headline.purpose: Page titles, game names on game pages, the name on the Who goes first reel and the dice total.

title.purpose: Section headings, modal headings, and the group name in the top bar from 900px.

title-small.purpose: Sub-section headings; at body weight, the lead size for intros, pick results and the 52px picker button.

box-title.purpose: Titles printed on box fronts, sized from the box width.

spine-title.purpose: Titles along spines in the Spines view.

label.purpose: Form labels, hints, small buttons, list facts.

caption.purpose: Cube captions, tags, bottom tab labels, dice captions; tabular figures.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: A box off its shelf: hovered or focused cube, pulled picker boxes and fillers, game-page hero box.

shadows.name: lift-dark
shadows.purpose: The lift shadow in dark mode.

shadows.name: box-hairline
shadows.purpose: Printed edge of box fronts and spines.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Shared curve for lifts, slides, the picker pull, the modal rise and the dice tumble.

motion.name: control
motion.purpose: Button colour and press transitions; pressed buttons drop 1px.

motion.name: cube-lift
motion.purpose: Box rises with the lift shadow on hover or focus.

motion.name: spine-slide
motion.purpose: Spine slides right on hover or focus.

motion.name: picker-pull
motion.value: 0.55s, translateY(28px) scale(0.96) to rest, 70ms stagger, tilts -2.5deg / 1.75deg / -1.25deg; hover straightens and lifts 4px over 0.25s
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: three boxes pulled off the shelf. Fillers take the same rise and stagger but stay straight and lift 3px on hover. No animation and no tilt under reduced motion.

motion.name: modal-rise
motion.purpose: A modal or bottom sheet opening. Still under reduced motion.

motion.name: reel-spin
motion.value: 2.3s, cubic-bezier(0.12, 0.6, 0.22, 1) to 86% with a 0.22-row overshoot, then ease-in-out back
motion.purpose: Who goes first: names roll up a 64px-row reel and settle on the pick. Under reduced motion the name shows without the roll.

motion.name: dice-tumble
motion.purpose: A rerolled die tumbles in. The coin face flips in over 0.35s (rotateX 90deg). Both still under reduced motion.

motion.name: skeleton-sweep
motion.value: 1.6s ease-in-out infinite, 90 to 120ms stagger between neighbours
motion.purpose: A band of light crossing shelf-gap placeholders while content loads; still under reduced motion.

motion.name: search-look
motion.purpose: The label-strip magnifier looks around while a search runs; still under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global rule under prefers-reduced-motion; looping animations stop rather than flicker.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Cube Shelf"**

The catalog is drawn as the group's shared cube-storage shelf. Each game is a box standing in its own square cube; the cubes sit in a grid separated by grey shelf gaps; the front edge of every cube is painted in the player colours of the people who own the game. Filters live on a dark shelf label above the grid. The ground is pale laminate, the ink is near-black, and almost everything else is low-chroma cardboard, so the owner edges are the only saturated colour on the shelf.

Density follows the use: three cubes across on a phone at the table, five to seven on a desktop at home, and a denser Spines view (boxes lying on their sides) for scanning long collections. The type is one family, Archivo, used heavy and semi-condensed for anything printed on a box and at normal width for interface text. Dark mode is the same shelf in black-brown laminate, with the same roles swapped value for value.

The world refuses the category default for game catalogs: a dark app with a grid of box-art cards and a filter sidebar. Box art from BoardGameGeek appears inside the cube when a game has it, hotlinked and cover-fitted, never copied; games without art get a printed box front so a hand-entered shelf still looks like a shelf.
keyCharacteristics: Square cubes on a shelf-gap grid, each closed by a 6px owner-colour edge.
Pale laminate ground, near-black ink, one dark label strip per screen for filters and search.
Player colours by join order are the only saturated colour; marigold marks what is chosen.
Printed box fronts in cardboard tones with a lid seam and a heavy condensed title.
Archivo alone, steered by weight (400 to 800) and width (78% to 100%).
Flat at rest; a box lifts with one soft shadow when touched, and the picker tilts three boxes off the shelf.

rules.name: The Marigold Means Chosen Rule
rules.body: Marigold appears only on something the person has turned on: an active filter, the current tab, a selected person, selected text, a focused field in the label strip. It never decorates, never marks ownership, and never fills a button.

rules.name: The Owner Edge Rule
rules.body: Player colours are the only saturated colour on the shelf, and they always mean a person. Assign them by join order, never by preference or by game, and never add a player colour that shares a hue with marigold.

rules.name: The Cardboard Print Rule
rules.body: A box front without art is a low-chroma cardboard print outside the player hues, light in most cases, dark in no more than about a quarter, and every print-and-ink pair is at least 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Printed Title Rule
rules.body: Anything that stands for a physical box (box fronts, spines, the hero box) sets its title at 800 and 78 to 80% width. Interface headings stay at 88% width and 780 or lighter, so the printed voice is reserved for the boxes.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo carries every role. Hierarchy comes from weight and the width axis; no second family, no letter-spaced uppercase labels. The join code is the one tracked-out uppercase setting, because it is a code people read aloud.

rules.name: The Shelf Gap Rule
rules.body: Cubes are separated by the shelf-gap colour showing between them, not by borders or shadows. A new grid of games sits on the same gap ground.

rules.name: The Thumb Reach Rule
rules.body: Below 900px the group tabs are a fixed bottom bar with 52px targets and safe-area padding; the filter row scrolls sideways in one line rather than wrapping. Tap targets are 44px for buttons and search, 38px for filter chips, 40px for person toggles.

rules.name: The Lift On Touch Rule
rules.body: Only a box gets a shadow, and only when it is off the shelf: touched, pulled, or shown on its own page. Panels, buttons and chips stay flat.

dos: Do put every grid of games on the shelf-gap ground with 6px gaps (8px from 760px) and close each cube with the owner edge.
Do take player colours from `playerColor()` by join order and box prints from `boxColor()` by name; both live in `src/lib/catalog/colors.ts`.
Do keep marigold for state: active filters, the current tab, selected people, text selection and focused label-strip fields.
Do set box and spine titles at 800 and 78 to 80% width, and interface headings at 780 and 88%.
Do hotlink BGG box art and fall back to the printed front when it is missing or fails to load.

Do render the footer on every page, including new routes outside the root layout. It carries the BGG credit whenever the instance shows BGG data; an instance that has never had BGG on shows only Privacy, Source and the theme select.
Do give any new motion a reduced-motion state with no animation and no tilt.
donts: Don't use marigold for facts. The picker's "Best at N" tag is a neutral cube-white tag with a rule outline, and the cube mark's second box is kraft cardboard, not marigold.
Don't use marigold for decoration, emphasis, ownership or a primary button.
Don't add a saturated colour to the shelf other than the owner edges, and don't add a player colour near marigold's hue.
Don't add a box print that is saturated, sits in a player hue, or falls below 4.5:1 with its ink; keep dark prints to about a quarter of the set.
Don't download, proxy or re-host BGG box art.
Don't put eyebrows or kickers (small uppercase labels) above headings.
Don't use hard offset shadows; the lift shadow is the only shadow.
Don't separate cubes with borders or card shadows; the shelf gap does that.
